For R-3 : Mr. M.Saravanan  ORDER This Criminal Revision Case has been filed to call for the records pertaining to the impugned order dated 03.09.2022 passed in C.M.P. No. 7713 of 2022 in C.C. No.1 of 2014 on the file of the learned Judicial Magistrate No.I, Kuzhithurai and to set aside the same.
2.
The facts in brief:
The third respondent is the defacto complainant.

He has filed complaint before the respondent Police with following allegations; that the marriage between the first accused namely Santhosh and the third respondent took place on 19.05.2010 as per the Christian Customs and rites.
At that time of marriage, she was provided with sufficient sridhana articles, jewellery apart from cash, extra.
Some house utilities things were also given by the parents of the third respondent at the time of house warming function to the accused 2 and 3.
Because of the above said marriage, a male child https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis was born on 09.07.2011.
Even before the marriage, the third respondent has completed Ph.D degree in Kerala University.
Over the above said educational qualification, she was harassed and irritated.
Later, the husband pledged the jewels belong to her for loan and started demanding more dowry.
But that was refused by her parents.
On 27.05.2012 the accused demanding more dowry pushed her out of the house.
On 18.06.2012 the first accused and his brother assaulted the third respondent demanding more dowry, due to which, she suffered by injury.
After that, there was compromise in the presence of elders and so she was taken to her matrimonial home on 27.07.2012.
Even after that the harassment did not stop.
Even for a simple issue, she was scolded, again she was driven out of the house by assault.
Due to the above said assault, she was taking treatment as inpatient in the Government hospital, Kuzhithurai.

At that time,
statement was also recorded by the Police.
At that time, the husband of the fourth accused namely Ragu who was working in the Police Department advised her to go to Marthandam Police Station.
Again there was compromise in the presence of elders and she was taken to the matrimonial home.
On 19.11.2012 at about 4.00 p.m., the sister of the first accused namely Sheeja came to the house, she instigated the first accused to drive the third respondent from the house.
All the accused joined together and demanded https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Rs.1,00,000/- as cash and apart from jewellery, she was assaulted by the first accused and also took her jewellery.

The accused Nos. 2 and 3 assaulted, pushed her out the house, the accused no.4 also C.Sathiyanesan vs The Inspector Of Police on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170592322/
2 assaulted on her head and accused no.5 caused assault with his leg.

sentences.text: 3. Over the above said occurrence, she has given a complaint before Marthandam Police Station on 14.11.2012, but there was no enquiry.
Now she is living with her parents.

On the basis of the above said complaint, a case was registered in Crime No.19 of 2013 for the offence under Sections 498(A),
420, 294(b), 323, 506(i) of IPC and the investigation was completed.
During the course of investigation, involvement of first accused alone was noticed and name of the all other accused were deleted in the Final Report.
4. The trial process was started on the basis of the Final Report, P.W.1 defacto complainant was examined in chief on 31.10.2019, repeated the very same allegations mentioned in her complaint.
On the side of the prosecution P.W.2 is her father and P.W.3 is her mother were examined in chief.
At that time no cross examination was made.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5.

The prosecution has moved a petition under Section 319 Cr.P.C. to add these petitioners as additional accused that is resisted by the first accused stating that the proposed accused Nos. 2 to 5 did not involve in the above such occurrence.
But however, the trial Court allowed the above said petition.
Challenging the above said only, this revision has been preferred.
6. Heard both sides.

7. At the outset, the learned counsel for the revision petitioner would submit that absolutely these petitioners were not involved in the issue between the husband and wife, since they are living separetely in a separate house.
Absolutely, there was no possibility for these petitioners to join with the first accused, cause assault and demand dowry to the defacto complainant.

Originally, the final report that was filed by the Investigation Officer stating that in the course of investigation, it was found that the defacto complainant and the first accused were residing separetely and he only received the sridhana articles, jewellery from the defacto complainant.
The accused Nos.2 and 3 constructed a separate house for the first accused and the defacto complainant.

In that house only,
the husband and wife were living.
The fourth accused namely Sheeja married on 2004 and living with https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis her husband.
Fifth accused namely Ananth also got married in 2008.
8. After the marriage between the defacto complainant and the first accused, they were living separetely.
Therefore, we find that the accused Nos.2 to 5 are no way involved in the above said assault, demanding dowry, extra.
From the investigation, it is seen that the defacto complainant and first accused living separetely in the house, which was constructed by the accused Nos.2 and 3.
The accused Nos.4 and 5 were already married and living seperately.
At this juncture, it appears that trouble arose between the husband and wife.
For the above said issue between the husband and wife, in-laws also been implicated.
In usual course, the in-laws are implicated in the matrimonial issue more or less in all the case has been noted, in the judgment of Honourable Supreme Court reported in Preethi Gupta's Case.

sentences.text: Not only the Investigation Officer and also the Court should be more carefull while scrutinising the evidence in the form of statement while in-laws are implicated.
Already there is a report by him noting non- involvement of these revision petitioners in the said issue.
But however as mentioned above, the defacto complainant is consistently stating that these petitioners are also involved in such harassment, demand of dowry.

When https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the second and third accused are living in a separate house in their own cost, how they could be implicated for demanding dowry and additional cash will make the allegation as improbable, unnatural also.
So also the accused Nos. 4 and 5 were already married and living separetely.

In this facts and circumstance of this case, the judgment of honourable Supreme Court in Preeti Gupta and another Vs. State of Jharkand and another reported in (2010) 7 SCC 667 is relevant for consideration that false implication cannot be ruled out.

entities.text: Preeti Gupta and another Vs. State of Jharkand and another reported in (2010) 7 SCC 667
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. Further the learned counsel for the revision petitioner would rely upon the above judgment for the purpose of argument that mere bald allegation is not enough to add additional accused.
There must be cogent and convincing reason and circumstances must be brought on record.
Here, except the allegation made in the complaint, no other circumstances, worth considering is brought on record during the course of trial by the defacto complainant.
11. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent would rely upon the judgment of honourable Supreme Court in Hardeep Singh Vs. State of Punjab and others (2014) 3 SCC 92.

entities.text: Hardeep Singh Vs. State of Punjab and others (2014) 3 SCC 92
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Subsequent to the above said https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis judgment, another case was referred to the co-ordinate Bench for answering this question with regard to the question as to the stage of the trial when Section 319 of Cr.P.C. Can be invoked.
12. At this juncture only, the opinion of honourable Supreme Court in Preethi Kupta's case got to be complied.
Except the bald statement of P.W.1 to 3 with regard to the alleged role against all these petitioners, no other material is brought on record during the course of trial.
So, implication of these petitioners are made by the P.W.1 to P.W.3 with ulterior motive.
The criminal prosecution could not be made as a weapon of oppression or vindication.
13. So, I am of the considered view that the substantial evidence is not brought on record to add these petitioners as additional accused.

If the trial Court is of the view that these petitioners to be tried, the judgment of honourable Supreme Court in Sukhpal Singh Khaira VS. The State of Punjab in Crliminal Appeal No.885 of 2019 dated 05.12.2022, must be followed, if fresh material is brought on record.

entities.text: Sukhpal Singh Khaira VS. The State of Punjab
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 14.
This revision is liable to be allowed.
Order in C.M.P.No.7713 of 2022 is set-aside with the above observation and liberty.
Consequently, the connected Miscellaneous Petition is closed.
